failures.criterion: A5: a Claude Code session carries the answer word for word at its start, resume, compaction and subagent start (and the plan's Claude path for A8)
failures.evidence: The answers hook (packages/claude-envoy/hooks/session-hook.ts, ANSWERS_BY_MS = 800, remainingUntil() counted from performance.now()'s origin) counts bun's own start-up against its 800 ms budget. Claude Code starts the open-asks, dispatch-first and answers hooks at the same time as itself, so on this pod the answers hook often reaches readSessionAnswers with deadlineMs 0. It then carries the failure line or a stale cached list, even when Dispatch answers at once, and it exits before the read can write answers.json. Observed on the real binary (Claude Code 2.1.311, `bun test tests/answers-claude.test.ts`): 3 of 3 runs failed at least one moment (resume, then compaction). In a probe copy of that test, round 2 of the second batch: Turn one carried `[Dispatch: people's answers from the last 72 hours could not be read (Dispatch did not answer within 0 ms); run `dispatch answers`.]`, while the stand-in Dispatch answered at once. The reason it names is false: Dispatch was given no time. Red test, its own commit: packages/claude-envoy/tests/answers-hook.test.ts, "a hook whose start-up took past 800 ms still carries the list Dispatch answers at once". A --preload holds the process to 820 ms, then Dispatch answers at once. Fails today: `cd packages/claude-envoy && bun test tests/answers-hook.test.ts -t 'start-up took past'` received `[Dispatch: people's answers from the last 72 hours could not be read (Dispatch did not answer within 0 ms); run `dispatch answers`.]` where the fresh list was expected.
